title: The Ice Pick Surgery That Won a Nobel Prize

sections.name: The Ice Pick Surgery That Won a Nobel Prize
lines: In the 1940s, an American doctor named Walter Freeman travelled the country performing a ten minute brain operation.
It was called the transorbital lobotomy. His tool looked a lot like an ice pick.
He pushed it in above the eye, and swept it side to side to cut connections in the front of the brain.
A different version of lobotomy even won its inventor a Nobel Prize, in 1949.
Some patients became calmer. Many were left changed forever, and some died.
New medicines arrived in the 1950s, and lobotomy fell out of use. Freeman performed around three and a half thousand of them.
